result: 2 approval-ready native taxa; 1 strict target-zone FAIL recommended as lookalike comparison

study_strategy.family_look_here_first: First ask evergreen or deciduous, then compare leaf size/texture and margin. Fruit color alone is weak because all three can carry red drupes. Confirm alternate simple leaves, dioecious flowers, and fleshy drupes with pyrenes.

quick_key.if: deciduous + larger thin crenate leaves + red fruit left on bare winter twigs
evergreen shrub/small tree + tiny leathery leaves with fine rounded crenate teeth
evergreen tree + much larger thick leaves with stiff sharp spine-tipped teeth
quick_key.then: Ilex opaca — strict target-zone FAIL / comparison candidate

family_traits: plants usually dioecious, so only female plants fruit
superior ovary develops into a fleshy drupe
drupe contains several hard pyrenes rather than a single stone
fruit often persists into winter and is useful only when combined with leaf/twig characters
priority_comparisons: Ilex decidua vs Ilex vomitoria — deciduous larger thin leaves vs evergreen tiny leathery leaves
Ilex vomitoria vs Ilex opaca — small low-crenate leaves vs large spine-tipped leaves
wild Ilex vs landscape cultivars — do not infer nativity from ornamental occurrence
